title: Beyond the 956: Óscar 'Patroncito' Cortez, undefeated Mexican boxing champion, dies at 20

content:
🌎 BEYOND THE 956

Óscar Gabriel Cortez Arredondo, known in the ring as “Patroncito,” the undefeated Mexican lightweight and reigning national champion, has died at 20.

His death was confirmed on Friday, November 13, by his trainer, Alfredo Caballero, and his promoter, Coliseo Promotions. No cause of death has been disclosed.

Born in Hermosillo and raised in Nogales, Sonora, Cortez was one of Mexican boxing’s brightest young prospects. A member of Caballero’s Team, he never lost a professional fight, winning the lightweight championship of the Federación de Comisiones de Boxeo de la República Mexicana (Fecombox) on February 21, 2026, with a decision over Luis “Sismo” Corona. His last fight came in June 2026, a win over Jonathan Isaac Uribe Hernández at Arena Sonora in Hermosillo.

Coliseo Promotions shared a farewell to the young champion on social media, and tributes poured in from across Mexican boxing for the 20-year-old who had been rising fast through the ranks.

Sources: RÉCORD; Mediotiempo; Claro Sports; TVyNovelas.
